name: Asthma
definition: A chronic inflammatory disease of the airways causing reversible narrowing, with episodes of wheeze, breathlessness, chest tightness and cough.
overview: In asthma the bronchial lining is chronically inflamed and over-reactive. Triggers such as allergens, viruses, exercise or cold air make the smooth muscle constrict and the lining swell and pour out mucus. Between attacks breathing may be normal. It affects about one child in ten and one adult in twelve.
causes: Genetic susceptibility plus environmental exposure: allergens (dust mite, pollen, pets), early viral infections, tobacco smoke, air pollution, occupational chemicals
riskFactors: Family history of asthma or allergy
signs: Fast breathing, use of accessory muscles in an attack
A silent chest and exhaustion in a life-threatening attack
complications: Side effects of repeated steroid courses
diagnosis: Variable symptoms plus evidence of variable airflow obstruction: spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility, peak-flow variability, or raised exhaled nitric oxide and blood eosinophils.
treatment: Inhaled corticosteroids are the foundation, combined with a long-acting bronchodilator as needed; a reliever inhaler for symptoms; a written action plan; trigger avoidance; biologic injections for severe allergic or eosinophilic asthma. Attacks are treated with high-dose reliever, oral steroids and oxygen.
prevention: Avoid smoking and smoke exposure, control allergens, have flu vaccination, use the preventer inhaler daily and check inhaler technique.
seekCare: Emergency care if the reliever is not helping, the person cannot speak in sentences, lips are blue, or peak flow is below a third of best.

sections.body:
First paragraph of plain prose, two to four sentences, each a claim that the sources you retrieved support.

Second paragraph after a blank line. No markdown, no bullet characters, no bold. At least 200 characters per section; aim for 110 to 220 words.

sections.heading: EXAMPLE FORMAT ONLY: What causes it?
sections.body: Plain prose again. Headings are phrased the way people search: a question or a short noun phrase. Between four and seven sections for a condition, each answering one thing people ask.

sections.heading: EXAMPLE FORMAT ONLY: When should you get medical help?
sections.body: Say who to contact and how fast: call 999 for emergencies, NHS 111 or the GP the same day for urgent problems, a routine GP appointment otherwise. Describe; do not instruct about medicines.

faqs.q: EXAMPLE FORMAT ONLY: Can this condition be cured?
faqs.a: A short, direct answer of 40 to 90 words that stands on its own, drawn from the same sources as the sections.
